evidence: rule_sets.py:326-327 builds exp.CurrentSchema() wrapped in CAST AS BINARY. The sqlglot source (pinned 30.31.0, requirements.txt:103) is not in the view, so I did not read its generator. The repo's unit tests expect the MySQL-dialect output to be SCHEMA(): tests/unit/test_safety_rule_sets.py:322,331,335,339,351 expect `CAST(`TABLE_SCHEMA` AS BINARY) = CAST(SCHEMA() AS BINARY)`. I did not run them. MySQL documents SCHEMA() as a synonym of DATABASE(). It returns the default (connected) database name, and information_schema TABLE_SCHEMA holds the same schema names. The claim holds on that basis. The BINARY casts on both sides make the comparison byte-exact.

src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py:321-323 builds exp.Cast(this=node, to=DataType.build('BINARY', dialect=_DIALECT)). tests/unit/test_safety_rule_sets.py:322-340 assert the generated MySQL SQL is e.g. CAST(`TABLE_SCHEMA` AS BINARY) = CAST(SCHEMA() AS BINARY). The existence check in src/sqllens/safety/relations.py:173-174 uses `WHERE BINARY schema = BINARY arg AND BINARY name = BINARY arg`. In MySQL, BINARY expr is defined as shorthand for CAST(expr AS BINARY), so both compare byte for byte. I did not run sqlglot; the generated text rests on the test expectations.

_catalog_body (src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py:373-391) builds the projection only by iterating spec.fields (lines 376-381). A field in `fields` becomes a real quoted column if it is in spec.kept, otherwise `NULL AS field`. A field omitted from `fields` is never projected, so it disappears from SELECT *, as the comment says. The projection uses only the static _CATALOG_VIEWS, with no rule-set input. _catalog_filter varies by rule set but only filters rows. Adding a field to `kept` therefore exposes its real value under every rule set, for the rows the filter allows. Absolute-claim input traced: a field added to `kept` that is also in `fields` (e.g. COLUMNS.COLUMN_DEFAULT) is projected as a real column for any rule set. A `kept` entry absent from `fields` is never projected, but the comment speaks of a view's fields, and every current kept entry is in fields.

rule_sets.py:143-146 sets _MATERIALIZE_LIMIT = "18446744073709551615" (2^64-1), the documented maximum LIMIT argument in MySQL. I checked the merge and pushdown claims against MySQL 8.0 documentation as I remember it. I did not run MySQL, and the repository view has no MySQL source or docs to read. The optimizer docs list LIMIT among the constructs that prevent merging a derived table (the same list as aggregates, DISTINCT, GROUP BY and UNION). They also say derived-condition pushdown (8.0.22+) is not done when the derived table has LIMIT. The derived_merge=on switch does not override this, so the counterexample I traced, a merge-enabled setting, still materializes a LIMIT-bearing derived table. Dropping the LIMIT would therefore allow merge or pushdown, as the comment says.

In src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py, _catalog_view (227-238) returns a view only for a db-qualified information_schema.{TABLES,COLUMNS,KEY_COLUMN_USAGE} reference with no catalog qualifier and a plain Identifier. Every other table reference goes to _check_reference (211-224). That function refuses any catalog or db qualifier (215-219: KIND_CATALOG for schemas in _CATALOG_SCHEMAS, otherwise KIND_QUALIFIED_TABLE), so information_schema.PROCESSLIST, mysql.user, sys.* and performance_schema.* are all refused, and so is a three-part catalog.db.name form. An unqualified name must be in the rule set's `tables` (223-224) and is otherwise refused. An unqualified listed name resolves to a base table in the connected database, not a catalog relation. Table functions and DUAL are refused (213-222). _analyze (276-282) also runs _check_reference on any table scope analysis missed. Trace of the unqualified and wrong-schema inputs: neither reaches a catalog view. information_schema.PROCESSLIST is refused as KIND_CATALOG. Nothing found lets another catalog relation through.

In src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py, _parse (177-197) refuses anything that is not an exp.Query (line 188), so SHOW, DESCRIBE, EXPLAIN and USE are refused. It also refuses TABLE shorthand, nested DML/DDL, SELECT INTO and JSON_TABLE. _analyze (249-283) walks every scope's table sources. A source is allowed only if _catalog_view (227-238) matches information_schema.TABLES, COLUMNS or KEY_COLUMN_USAGE, or if _check_reference (211-224) finds it listed in the rule set. _check_reference refuses any other qualified name (lines 215-219). That covers mysql, performance_schema, sys and any other information_schema view, with KIND_CATALOG or KIND_QUALIFIED_TABLE. An unqualified unlisted name is refused as KIND_UNLISTED_TABLE. Test input: a SELECT from information_schema.PROCESSLIST, a schema-qualified mysql.user, or a SHOW statement. Each is refused. The guard raises RuleSetRefusal on any exception, so it fails closed (590-596). The three allowed views are rewritten to filtered derived tables, so they are still SELECTs against the named views. I found no path that lets another catalog read through. Scalar functions such as DATABASE() are not catalog lookups, and assert_no_denied_functions also runs on the rewritten SQL (577).

_catalog_body (src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py:373-391) builds the derived table body as SELECT ... The base-table path _derived is the other use, and the claim names the catalog body. MySQL's documented optimizer rules say a derived table containing LIMIT cannot be merged into the outer query. Absolute-claim input traced: a model WHERE with a side-effecting or erroring expression on the outer query. It stays in the outer block over the materialized rows, because there is no merge and no pushdown. I did not run MySQL, so the optimizer behavior rests on the documented rules.
